topic.name: Calculating the Equation of a Tangent Line Using Differentiation

question.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=2x^2+8x$ at the point $(2,24).$
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=2x^2+8x.$ Computing the derivative $f'(x)$ gives

\begin{align*} f'(x) = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(2x^2 + 8x\right)= 4x+8. \end{align*}

We then compute $f'(2)$, which gives \begin{align*} f'(2) = 4(2)+8 = 16 \,. \end{align*}

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=16$ and the coordinates of our point $(2, 24),$ and get \begin{align*} y - y_1 &= m(x-x_1) \\ y - (24) &= 16(x-2) \\ y & = 16x - 32 +24\\ y &= 16x-8. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Equation of a Tangent Line to a Curve at a Point

question.text: Find where the tangent to the curve $y = x^5+2$ at the point $(-1,1)$ intersects the $x$-axis.
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=x^5+2.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

\begin{align*} f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^5+2\right) = 5x^4 \end{align*}

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is \begin{align*} m=f'(-1) = 5(-1)^4 = 5. \\ \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

\begin{align} y - y_1 &= m(x-x_1) \\ y - 1 &= 5(x+1) \\ y & = 5x+5+1\\ y &= 5x+6. \end{align}

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $x$-axis, we set $y=0$ and solve:

\begin{align*} 0 & = 5x+6\\ x & = -\dfrac{6}{5} \end{align*}

Therefore, the point of intersection is $\left(-\dfrac{6}{5}, 0\right).$

example.title: Determining where a Tangent Line Intersects an Axis

question.text: Find where the tangent to the curve $y = \dfrac{2}{x} + x$ at the point  $(2,3)$ intersects the $x$-axis.
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=\dfrac{2}{x} + x.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

\begin{align*} f'(x) &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(\dfrac{2}{x} + x\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right) + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(2x^{-1}\right) + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x\right) \\[5pt] &= -2x^{-2} + 1 \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2}{x^{2}} + 1. \end{align*}

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is \begin{align*} m &= f'(2) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2}{2^{2}} + 1 \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2}{4} + 1 \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{2} + 1 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

\begin{align*} y - y_{1} &= m(x-x_{1}) \\[5pt] y - 3 &= \dfrac{1}{2}(x-2) \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{1}{2}x - 1 + 3 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{1}{2}x + 2. \end{align*}

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $x$-axis, we set $y=0$ and solve:

\begin{align*} \dfrac{1}{2}x + 2 &= 0 \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{2}x &= -2 \\[5pt] x &= -2\cdot 2 \\[5pt] x &= -4 \end{align*}

Therefore, the point of intersection is $\left(\bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{-4}, \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}\right).$
